basis: Developmental impairment, epilepsy, abnormal tone and cerebral abnormalities define a neurologic disorder; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Marrow failure and mucocutaneous diagnostic triad; cirrhosis in 1/2 patients supports hepatic involvement; neurologic abnormalities in 1/2 omitted because of cap.
Polycystic lesions of bone define the disease; no evidence supports another organ axis.
Benign tumour originating in parathyroid endocrine tissue; skeletal and renal complications belong to associated hyperparathyroidism.
Viral infection directly involving the central nervous system; additional organs are not consistently affected across this umbrella.
UV-related skin disease; progressive neurodegeneration commonly exceeds 50% in XP-A; damaging ocular surface disease and sensorineural hearing loss each occur in roughly 30% or more.
Marrow hypocellularity and anemia define marrow failure; associated hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent infections support intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Familial cutaneous capillary ectasia defines the skin vascular disorder; oropharyngeal cancer is a separately diagnosed predisposition outcome; caries is a separate dental disease.
Inherited abnormal hemoglobin affects erythrocytes; systemic damage varies by subtype and does not apply to most patients across the umbrella.
Benign smooth muscle tumour arising in the kidney; smooth muscle histology does not indicate skeletal muscle disease.
GnRH deficiency defines endocrine disease; anosmia or hyposmia in 3/8 patients (~38%) supports olfactory neurologic involvement; dental and skeletal findings are below 30%.
Explicitly nonsyndromic early-onset cataract; the NHS gene does not justify importing features of other NHS-related syndromes.
Severe neonatal hyperparathyroidism; fractures and abnormal mineralization in 80-99%; aminoaciduria in 80-99% supports tubular dysfunction; organ enlargement alone is insufficient.
Carcinoma originates in the parotid salivary gland, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis; surrounding invasion is not universal.
Meningeal tumour at the jugular foramen; location near skull bone and vessels does not establish their direct involvement.
Ectopic implantation in a fallopian tube is an obstetric and reproductive condition outside the axes; hemorrhage is a complication.
Brittle, sparse hair defines the syndrome; intellectual disability is a characteristic, commonly reported feature (>30%); nail abnormalities share the dermatologic axis.
Inflammation directly affects brain parenchyma; infectious or immune-mediated causes account for most cases across this umbrella.
Antibody-mediated type II hypersensitivity defines an autoimmune mechanism; no single target organ applies across the category.
Congenital displacement of the urethral opening directly affects the urethra, which is included in the renal axis.
Sensory neuropathy and dementia define neurologic disease; progressive hearing loss is a defining feature, present in 16/18 patients.
Nonsyndromic severe to profound sensorineural hearing loss; no additional organ involvement is established.
Intellectual disability defines syndrome; PDA reported in 80-99% supports cardiac involvement; asthma/infections are separate illnesses; minor dysmorphisms lack established functional damage.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; hearing loss in 2/2 assessed supports ear involvement; feeding dependence and hypoventilation are neurologic sequelae; isolated optic/cardiac findings lack 30% support.
Spastic paraplegia, ataxia and intellectual disability define neurologic disease; urinary and eye-movement findings reflect neural dysfunction without established renal or ocular damage.
